# 2026-07-31 — nawagner (claude-code) — CI/test speed

Issue: #114 (filed this session)

## The question

"Is there any way to make the CI tests go faster so we can increase dev
velocity?"

## What I measured before changing anything

CI wall clock across the last 25 runs was 30–90s, so CI was not slow in
absolute terms. Worth saying plainly, because the instinct at that number is
to reach for parallelism, and parallelism was the wrong lever.

Per-step timing, run 30654679072, `test` job (42s):

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| `pip install -e ".[web,dev,pdf,docx]"` | 11s |
| `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` | 1s |
| `pytest` | 20s |
| `pytest -m integration` | 4s |
| `mypy` | 0s |

`worker` (20s) runs in parallel — not the critical path, left alone.

## The finding that mattered

Locally the default suite was **20.09s wall clock but 3.9s of CPU**. That gap
is the whole story: the suite was not computing, it was waiting. `--durations`
put ~17s of it in one file, `tests/test_checks_live.py`, which really calls
doi.org, Crossref, OpenAlex and arXiv.

Deleting that file from the run: **20.09s → 2.48s**, 391 tests still passing.

The live tests are deliberate and good — a mocked resolver agrees with our
idea of the outside world instead of the real one, which is the entire point
of the deterministic tier. They should keep running. They just should not sit
in the loop a developer hits dozens of times an hour.

The file's own docstring had already specced the fix and I took it nearly
verbatim, only preferring a marker over the `SLOPCHECK_LIVE=1` env var it
suggested, so it matches how `test_integration_e2e.py` already handles
`integration` (one mechanism, not two).

## What landed

1. **`pytestmark = pytest.mark.live`** on `tests/test_checks_live.py`;
   `addopts = "-m 'not integration and not live'"`; marker registered.
2. **Own CI job** (`live`), parallel with `test`, running `pytest -m live`.
3. **pip → uv** — measured 2.0s vs 18.0s cold on the same extras.
4. **`concurrency:` group** with cancel-in-progress everywhere except main.

## Why a separate job, not just a separate step

A separate *step* in `test` would have fixed the local loop but saved no CI
wall clock, and would have left the important problem in place. #43 is about
to make `test` a required check. Live tests inside a required check means a
Crossref rate limit or a doi.org blip blocks every merge on the repo. As its
own advisory job, an outage reds `live` and nothing else.

There is a comment in `ci.yml` saying so, because the failure mode here is
someone helpfully adding `live` to the `mainsaver` ruleset later and
reintroducing exactly the problem this removed.

## Results

- Local default `pytest`: **20.1s → 2.7s**
- Expect `test` job ~42s → ~10s; CI wall clock bounded by `live` (~25s)
- Coverage unchanged — all 432 tests still run in CI

## Dead ends / deliberate non-goals

- **pytest-xdist.** The reflexive fix, and wrong here. Post-gating the suite
  is 2.5s wall / 2.3s CPU; xdist worker startup would eat most of a 4-core
  runner's gain. Recorded in the issue so nobody re-derives it.
- **`paths:` filters** to skip jobs — `ci.yml` already warns why (a required
  check that never runs leaves a PR permanently pending). Didn't touch it.
- **Matrix on `test`** — same warning, renames the check. Adding a sibling
  job is safe; `test` keeps its name.
- **Caching the live responses** (VCR/cassettes) — considered and rejected.
  It would make them fast but would convert them into exactly the mocked
  tests the file exists to avoid. The value is that they can fail when the
  outside world changes.

## Side finding, not fixed

`mypy` in CI does nothing. `src/slopchecker/` has no `py.typed`, so mypy exits
with "Package 'slopchecker' cannot be type checked due to missing py.typed
marker" and `continue-on-error: true` hides it. That's why the step takes 0s.
Verified identical under both pip and uv, so it predates this change and the
installer swap neither causes nor fixes it.

Left alone on purpose: adding `py.typed` turns mypy on for real and surfaces a
backlog of type errors, which is not a CI-speed change and shouldn't ride in
on one. Worth its own issue.

## Next

- Watch a real run to confirm the uv and cache numbers on the runner
  (local measurements are a sandbox, not `ubuntu-latest`).
- When #43 is flipped: add `test` to the ruleset, **not** `live`.

input.title: #114 Gate live-network tests behind a marker; pip -> uv
input.head: claude/ci-test-performance-6splmf
input.body:
Closes #114.

## The measurement

CI wall clock was 30–90s, so CI wasn't slow in absolute terms — but the `test` job's `pytest` step was **20.09s wall clock against only 3.9s of CPU**. The suite wasn't computing, it was waiting. `--durations` put ~17.6s of that in one file: `tests/test_checks_live.py`, which really calls doi.org, Crossref, OpenAlex and arXiv.

Excluding that one file: **20.09s → 2.48s**, 391 tests still passing.

Per-step timing from run [30654679072](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/actions/runs/30654679072) (`test`, 42s): pip install 11s, ruff 1s, `pytest` 20s, integration 4s, mypy 0s. The `worker` job (20s) runs in parallel and isn't the critical path, so it's untouched.

## What changed

- **`pytestmark = pytest.mark.live`** on `tests/test_checks_live.py`, deselected via `addopts = "-m 'not integration and not live'"`, marker registered.
- **New `live` CI job** running `pytest -m live`, parallel to `test` rather than inside it.
- **pip → uv** for installs — measured 2.0s vs 18.0s cold on the same extras. Astral tooling is already in the stack via ruff.
- **`concurrency:` group** with cancel-in-progress everywhere except main.

The live tests are deliberate and stay — a mocked resolver agrees with our idea of the outside world instead of the real one, which is the whole point of the deterministic tier. They just shouldn't sit in the loop a developer hits dozens of times an hour. The file's own docstring already specced this fix; this takes it, preferring a marker over the `SLOPCHECK_LIVE=1` env var it suggested so it matches how `test_integration_e2e.py` already handles `integration` — one mechanism, not two.

## Why a separate job, not a separate step

A separate *step* would have fixed the local loop but saved no CI wall clock, and left the more important problem in place.

#43 is about to make `test` a required check. Live tests inside a required check means a Crossref rate limit or a doi.org blip blocks **every merge on the repo**. As its own advisory job, an outage reds `live` and nothing else.

⚠️ **Do not add `live` to the `mainsaver` ruleset** when #43 is flipped. There's a comment in `ci.yml` saying so, next to the two warnings already there — the failure mode is someone helpfully adding it later and reintroducing exactly what this removes.

`test` keeps its name, so #43's required-check wiring is unaffected.

## Verification

Local: default `pytest` **20.09s → 2.71s** (397 passed, 2 skipped, 33 deselected); `pytest -m live` 24 passed in 17.85s; `pytest -m integration` 7 passed / 2 skipped; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

Independently red-green verified by a separate agent against the vacuous-pass failure mode — a mistyped marker would select 0 tests, exit 0, and turn the `live` job green while testing nothing — plus a check that no test is orphaned out of all three selections, and that the default run genuinely makes no network calls.

Coverage is unchanged: all 432 tests still run in CI. 24 live + 9 integration just aren't on the critical path.

## Deliberately not done

- **pytest-xdist.** The reflexive fix, and wrong here — post-gating the suite is 2.5s wall / 2.3s CPU, so worker startup would eat most of a 4-core runner's gain. Not waiting on the network was the lever, not parallelism.
- **Cassettes/VCR for the live tests.** Would make them fast but convert them into exactly the mocked tests the file exists to avoid.
- **`paths:` filters or a matrix on `test`** — `ci.yml` already documents why both brick the required check.

## Side finding, not fixed here

`mypy` in CI is a silent no-op: `src/slopchecker/` has no `py.typed`, so it exits "Package 'slopchecker' cannot be type checked" and `continue-on-error: true` hides it. That's why the step takes 0s. Verified identical under pip and uv, so it predates this change and the installer swap neither causes nor fixes it. Left alone on purpose — turning mypy on surfaces a backlog of type errors, which shouldn't ride in on a speed change. Worth its own issue.

---

The default "unit" suite was 20.09s wall clock but only 3.9s of CPU. The
gap was network wait, and ~17.6s of it was one file: tests/test_checks_live.py
really calls doi.org, Crossref, OpenAlex and arXiv. Excluding it takes the
suite to 2.48s with 391 tests still passing.

Those live tests are deliberate and stay — a mocked resolver agrees with our
idea of the outside world instead of the real one. They just shouldn't sit in
the loop a developer hits dozens of times an hour. The file's own docstring
already specced this fix; this takes it, preferring a marker over the
SLOPCHECK_LIVE env var it suggested so it matches how test_integration_e2e.py
already handles `integration`.

- pytestmark = pytest.mark.live, deselected via addopts, marker registered
- new `live` CI job running in parallel with `test`, not inside it
- pip -> uv for installs: measured 2.0s vs 18.0s cold, same extras
- concurrency group so superseded pushes stop holding runner slots

The separate job matters most for #43. Once `test` is a required check, a
Crossref rate limit inside it would block every merge on the repo; as its own
advisory job an outage reds `live` and nothing else. ci.yml carries a comment
saying not to add `live` to the mainsaver ruleset, alongside the two warnings
already there.

`test` keeps its name, so the required-check wiring in #43 is unaffected.

Coverage is unchanged: all 432 tests still run in CI, 24 live + 9 integration
just aren't on the critical path. Local pytest 20.1s -> 2.7s.

No pytest-xdist on purpose — at 2.5s wall / 2.3s CPU the worker startup would
eat the gain. Not waiting on the network was the lever, not parallelism.

input.title: test_report_pdf.py is ~11s of a 16s CI unit run (headless Chrome)
input.body:
Found while doing #114 (CI speed). Filing rather than fixing because `src/slopchecker/report/` is Emerson's module (→ Dominique).

## What

After #114 gated the live-network tests out of the default run, the CI `pytest` step is 16.01s — and per-file timestamps in the [job log](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/actions/runs/30655823101/job/91239830547) show **~11s of it is two tests**:

```
18:36:49.269  tests/test_report_html.py ..................  [ 93%]
18:37:00.304  tests/test_report_pdf.py ..                   [ 94%]
```

Everything else — 401 tests — runs in about 2s.

## Why it hid

`test_report_pdf.py` **skips locally** when no browser is present, so it never showed up in local `--durations` profiling. It only bites on CI, where ubuntu runners ship `google-chrome` on PATH (per #49) and the test really launches headless Chrome to render a PDF.

Worth naming as a general lesson: local profiling structurally could not see this one. I predicted the CI `pytest` step would drop to ~3s after #114 and it went to 16s; this file is the entire gap.

## Options (owner's call)

1. **Mark it `pdf` (or reuse `integration`) and give it its own parallel job**, same shape as #114's `live` job. Keeps the coverage, takes 11s off the critical path. Cheapest option and consistent with what's now there.
2. **Reuse one browser across both tests** if they currently launch separately — may recover a few seconds for free.
3. **Leave it.** 11s is not fatal and PDF is the shipping artifact per CLAUDE.md, so there's a real argument for keeping it in the required check. Recording the number is still worth it.

I lean (1), but it's a coverage-vs-speed tradeoff on the module that renders the actual deliverable, so it should be the owner's decision rather than a drive-by from a CI ticket.

## Current numbers for reference

`test` job after #114 is 35s: uv install 2s, ruff 0s, **`pytest` 16s**, `pytest -m integration` 4s, mypy 0s. Removing the PDF leg would put it near 24s, with `live` (~22s incl. setup) then setting the wall clock.

input.title: mypy in CI is a silent no-op — missing py.typed, masked by continue-on-error
input.body:
Found while doing #114. Not fixed there because turning mypy on is not a CI-speed change and shouldn't ride in on one.

## What

The `mypy` step in `ci.yml` has never type-checked anything. `src/slopchecker/` has no `py.typed` marker, so mypy resolves the installed package, refuses it, and exits **2**. `continue-on-error: true` (added in #2, reasonably, as "non-blocking to start") hides it, and the step reports green.

Straight from the [job log](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/actions/runs/30655823101/job/91239830547):

```
Package 'slopchecker' cannot be type checked due to missing py.typed marker.
See https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/installed_packages.html for more details
##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.
```

That's why the step takes 0s — it isn't fast, it's doing nothing.

Verified identical under both `pip install -e` and `uv pip install --system`, so it predates #114 and the installer swap neither causes nor fixes it.

## Fix

`mypy` is configured with `packages = ["slopchecker"]`, which makes it resolve the *installed* distribution and hit the `py.typed` rule. Two routes:

1. **Add `src/slopchecker/py.typed`** (empty file) + `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] force-include` or equivalent so it ships. Correct if we ever want the package to advertise its types to consumers.
2. **Point mypy at the source tree instead** — `files = ["src/slopchecker"]` rather than `packages`. Simpler, no packaging implications, and matches what the check is actually for here.

Either way, expect a backlog of real type errors to surface on the first honest run — the codebase has never been checked. That's the actual work in this ticket, and it's why it wants its own PR.

## Then decide on continue-on-error

Once it type-checks for real, `continue-on-error: true` is the thing to revisit. #2 called it "non-blocking to start"; this is the moment that note was written for. Suggest: fix the errors, then drop the flag so it can't silently rot again.

---

input.body:
## Real-runner results — and a correction

Run [30655823101](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/actions/runs/30655823101), all three jobs green. **One of my predicted numbers was wrong**, so here are the measured ones.

### `test` job — 35s (was 42s)

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| install | 11s (pip) | **2s (uv)** ✅ |
| ruff check + format | 1s | 0s |
| `pytest` | 20s | **16s** ❌ predicted ~3s |
| `pytest -m integration` | 4s | 4s |
| mypy | 0s | 0s |

### `live` job — 22s, running in parallel

```
24 passed, 1 skipped, 412 deselected, 1 warning in 10.36s
```

Not a vacuous pass: 24 tests really selected and really ran on the runner.

### Where I was wrong

I predicted the `pytest` step would fall to ~3s. It went to 16s. The gating is working exactly as designed — `403 selected, 33 deselected` (24 live + 9 integration) — but ~11s of the remaining 16s is **two tests in `tests/test_report_pdf.py`**:

```
18:36:49.269  tests/test_report_html.py ..................  [ 93%]
18:37:00.304  tests/test_report_pdf.py ..                   [ 94%]
```

The other 401 tests run in about 2s.

That file **skips locally** with no browser installed, so it never appeared in local `--durations` output. My local profiling structurally could not have caught it — the 20.1s → 2.7s local measurement is real, it just wasn't the whole CI picture. Filed as #118 for the module owner rather than fixed here, since `src/slopchecker/report/` is Emerson's (→ Dominique).

So the honest summary of this PR:

- **Local dev loop: 20.09s → 2.71s.** Unchanged claim, and it's the one that matters most for day-to-day velocity.
- **CI `test` job: 42s → 35s**, not the ~10s I projected. The uv half landed as predicted (11s → 2s); the pytest half is capped by the PDF tests until #118.
- **Flake isolation: delivered in full**, and that was always the load-bearing part given #43.

### Also confirmed on the runner

mypy's silent failure, now with receipts — `##[error]Process completed with exit code 2`, masked by `continue-on-error`. Filed as #120.

## Correction to the "Expected result" above

PR #117 is green on a real runner ([run 30655823101](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/actions/runs/30655823101)). One projection in the original post did not survive contact with it.

| Claim | Projected | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Local default `pytest` | ~2.5s | **2.71s** ✅ |
| uv install | ~2-3s | **2s** ✅ |
| CI `pytest` step | ~3s | **16s** ❌ |
| CI `test` job | ~10s | **35s** ❌ |

The gating is correct — `403 selected, 33 deselected`, and `live` reports `24 passed ... in 10.36s`, so nothing is vacuously passing. The miss is that **~11s of the remaining 16s is two tests in `tests/test_report_pdf.py`**, which launch headless Chrome on CI and **skip locally** when no browser is present. Local `--durations` could not see them, so my projection was built on a profile that was blind to the thing that now dominates. Filed as #118.

Net: the local-loop win is real and full-size (20.09s → 2.71s), the uv win is real, the flake isolation is real — but the CI wall-clock win is roughly 42s → 35s rather than the 4x I wrote above, and it stays there until #118 is decided by the report module's owner.

Leaving the original post unedited so the wrong number stays visible next to the right one.

Status while I wait on the red-green agent and the second CI run:

**PR [#117](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/pull/117) is open, issue [#114](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/issues/114) claimed and assigned to you.** First CI run was green on all three jobs.

**The real runner refuted one of my predictions**, so I corrected it on both the PR and the issue before merging:

| | Predicted | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Local `pytest` | ~2.5s | **2.71s** ✅ |
| uv install | ~2–3s | **2s** ✅ |
| CI `test` job | ~10s | **35s** ❌ |

The gating itself is correct — `403 selected, 33 deselected`, and the `live` job reports `24 passed ... in 10.36s`, so it isn't passing vacuously. The miss is that **~11s of the remaining 16s is two tests in `test_report_pdf.py`**, which launch headless Chrome on CI but *skip locally* when no browser is present. My local `--durations` profile was structurally blind to them — which is exactly why running it on a real runner was worth doing rather than merging on local numbers.

I did not fix that here: `src/slopchecker/report/` is Emerson's module (→ Dominique), and per CLAUDE.md that goes through them. Filed as [#118](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/issues/118) with the three options and my lean.

So the honest scorecard for this PR: local dev loop 20.09s → 2.71s (full-size, and the one that matters most hour-to-hour), uv 11s → 2s, flake isolation delivered in full — but CI wall clock is 42s → 35s, not the 4x I projected, until #118 is decided.

Two other things landed:
- **[#120](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/issues/120)** — mypy's silent no-op, now with runner receipts (`##[error]Process completed with exit code 2`, masked by `continue-on-error`). Confirmed identical under pip and uv, so it predates this change.
- **`.claude/worktrees/` added to `.gitignore`** — the stop hook flagged it as untracked; it's a full nested clone of the repo that my subagent's isolated worktree created, and committing it would have been bad. Session transcript committed alongside, per the tracked-transcripts convention.

I'll merge once the agent's verdict is in and the second run is green — unless the agent turns up something, in which case I'll bring it to you first.

Gate live-network tests behind a marker; pip -> uv

The default "unit" suite was 20.09s wall clock but only 3.9s of CPU. The
gap was network wait, and ~17.6s of it was one file: tests/test_checks_live.py
really calls doi.org, Crossref, OpenAlex and arXiv. Excluding it takes the
suite to 2.48s with 391 tests still passing.

Those live tests are deliberate and stay — a mocked resolver agrees with our
idea of the outside world instead of the real one. They just shouldn't sit in
the loop a developer hits dozens of times an hour. The file's own docstring
already specced this fix; this takes it, preferring a marker over the
SLOPCHECK_LIVE env var it suggested so it matches how test_integration_e2e.py
already handles `integration`.

- pytestmark = pytest.mark.live, deselected via addopts, marker registered
- new `live` CI job running in parallel with `test`, not inside it
- pip -> uv for installs: measured 2.0s vs 18.0s cold, same extras
- concurrency group so superseded pushes stop holding runner slots

The separate job matters most for #43. Once `test` is a required check, a
Crossref rate limit inside it would block every merge on the repo; as its own
advisory job an outage reds `live` and nothing else. ci.yml carries a comment
saying not to add `live` to the mainsaver ruleset, alongside the two warnings
already there.

`test` keeps its name, so the required-check wiring in #43 is unaffected.

Coverage is unchanged: all 432 tests still run in CI, 24 live + 9 integration
just aren't on the critical path. Local pytest 20.1s -> 2.7s.

No pytest-xdist on purpose — at 2.5s wall / 2.3s CPU the worker startup would
eat the gain. Not waiting on the network was the lever, not parallelism.

Gate live-network tests behind a marker; pip -> uv

The default "unit" suite was 20.09s wall clock but only 3.9s of CPU. The
gap was network wait, and ~17.6s of it was one file: tests/test_checks_live.py
really calls doi.org, Crossref, OpenAlex and arXiv. Excluding it takes the
suite to 2.48s with 391 tests still passing.

Those live tests are deliberate and stay — a mocked resolver agrees with our
idea of the outside world instead of the real one. They just shouldn't sit in
the loop a developer hits dozens of times an hour. The file's own docstring
already specced this fix; this takes it, preferring a marker over the
SLOPCHECK_LIVE env var it suggested so it matches how test_integration_e2e.py
already handles `integration`.

- pytestmark = pytest.mark.live, deselected via addopts, marker registered
- new `live` CI job running in parallel with `test`, not inside it
- pip -> uv for installs: measured 2.0s vs 18.0s cold, same extras
- concurrency group so superseded pushes stop holding runner slots

The separate job matters most for #43. Once `test` is a required check, a
Crossref rate limit inside it would block every merge on the repo; as its own
advisory job an outage reds `live` and nothing else. ci.yml carries a comment
saying not to add `live` to the mainsaver ruleset, alongside the two warnings
already there.

`test` keeps its name, so the required-check wiring in #43 is unaffected.

Coverage is unchanged: all 432 tests still run in CI, 24 live + 9 integration
just aren't on the critical path. Local pytest 20.1s -> 2.7s.

No pytest-xdist on purpose — at 2.5s wall / 2.3s CPU the worker startup would
eat the gain. Not waiting on the network was the lever, not parallelism.

Both merge preconditions are now down to one: the red-green agent is still running. Since you conditioned the merge on that verification passing, I'll hold the merge until its verdict lands rather than merging on the CI signal alone.

Where things stand:

- **PR [#117](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/pull/117)** — green on two consecutive runs, real-runner numbers posted, ready to merge pending the agent.
- **Issue [#114](https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/issues/114)** — claimed, assigned, and corrected where my projection was wrong.

The runner-side evidence against the failure mode I was most worried about is already in hand — `live` reported `24 passed, 1 skipped, 412 deselected in 10.36s`, so the marker is selecting real tests rather than silently selecting none. The agent is checking the harder version of that question: whether any test has fallen out of *all three* selections, which would be a silent coverage loss rather than a visible one.

I'll merge and report as soon as it comes back clean — or bring you its findings first if it turns up something real.

Committed and pushed (`4757c4c`) — working tree is clean.

## Red-green verification

The failure mode this change most plausibly introduces is a **vacuous pass**: a mistyped marker or a wrong selection expression makes `pytest -m live` collect 0 tests, exit 0, and turn the `live` job green while testing nothing. A test could also fall out of *all three* selections and silently stop running anywhere — a coverage loss that looks identical to a speedup.

Both are now tested rather than argued.

### 1. The three selections partition the suite exactly

```
total=432 default=399 live=24 integration=9 union=432
ORPHANED (in total, in no run): NONE
OVERLAP default&live: NONE
OVERLAP default&integration: NONE
OVERLAP live&integration: NONE
VERDICT: PARTITION CLEAN
```

Every test runs in exactly one family. Nothing orphaned, nothing double-counted. Confirmed independently on the runner, where the three steps report `403 selected / 33 deselected`, `24 selected / 412 deselected`, and `9 selected / 427 deselected` — all against the same 436 collected.

### 2. A broken live test really reds the `live` job

Flipped `test_real_doi_resolves` to assert the wrong `Outcome`:

```
FAILED tests/test_checks_live.py::test_real_doi_resolves - AssertionError
1 failed, 23 passed, 408 deselected in 23.92s
exit=1
```

### 3. A broken integration test really reds the step

Added a failing canary to `test_integration_e2e.py`:

```
FAILED tests/test_integration_e2e.py::test_sabotage_canary - AssertionError
1 failed, 7 passed, 2 skipped, 423 deselected in 2.86s
exit=1
```

Both sabotages reverted; `git diff tests/` is empty and the suite is back to `397 passed, 2 skipped, 33 deselected in 2.61s`.

### Verdict

The gating does what it claims: real tests are selected, failures propagate to the exit code, and no test was silently dropped. Merging.

# RED-GREEN verification: `claude/ci-test-performance-6splmf` (commit `d29d80d`)

**Setup:** detached checkout of `origin/claude/ci-test-performance-6splmf` in an isolated worktree; dedicated venv at `.venv` (`uv pip install -e ".[web,dev,pdf,docx]"`, pytest 9.1.1, Python 3.11.15) so the main worktree's editable install was never touched. Network available. All sabotage reverted; `git status` clean at exit.

| # | Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No vacuous pass | **CONFIRMED** (with one narrow residual shape) |
| 2 | No orphaned tests | **CONFIRMED** |
| 3 | Default run makes no network calls | **CONFIRMED** |
| 4 | Timing | **CONFIRMED** |
| 5 | Coverage equivalence | **REFUTED** |

---

## Claim 1 — VACUOUS PASS: CONFIRMED

**Live, RED:** planted `assert False, "SABOTAGE-CANARY-LIVE"` in `tests/test_checks_live.py::test_real_doi_resolves`.

```
$ .venv/bin/pytest -m live -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=line
FAILED tests/test_checks_live.py::test_real_doi_resolves - AssertionError: SA...
1 failed, 23 passed, 1 skipped, 404 deselected, 1 warning in 16.30s
PYTEST_EXIT=1
```
Non-zero count reported (24 selected), exit 1. With the same sabotage in place the default run stayed green (`393 passed … exit 0`), confirming the deselection is real in both directions.

**Integration, RED:** planted `assert False` in `test_integration_e2e.py::test_run_leg_exits_cleanly`.
```
$ .venv/bin/pytest -m integration -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=line -rs
FAILED tests/test_integration_e2e.py::test_run_leg_exits_cleanly
1 failed, 6 passed, 3 skipped, 419 deselected, 1 warning in 3.08s
PYTEST_EXIT=1
```

**The specific failure mode you named — mistyped marker → 0 selected → green — cannot happen.** I forced it three ways; pytest returns exit code 5 (`NO_TESTS_COLLECTED`) every time, which reds the CI job:

```
$ .venv/bin/pytest -m nonexistentmarker123 -q     → 1 skipped, 428 deselected   EXIT=5
$ .venv/bin/pytest -m liv -q                      → 1 skipped, 428 deselected   EXIT=5
# and with the source typo'd (pytestmark = pytest.mark.liv):
$ .venv/bin/pytest -m live -q                     → PytestUnknownMarkWarning    EXIT=5
```
Fail-safe in both directions: under the typo the file also falls *back into* the default run (`419/428 tests collected`, i.e. 395+24), so it is not orphaned either. Same for a genuinely absent optional dep — I uninstalled `pymupdf` and ran `pytest -m integration`: `1 skipped, 423 deselected`, **exit 5**, red.

**Residual caveat (not introduced by this change, pre-exists for `integration`):** exit 5 only fires on *zero collected*. If tests are collected but all skipped, exit is 0 and the job goes green testing nothing:
```
# pytestmark = [pytest.mark.live, pytest.mark.skipif(True, reason="...")]
$ .venv/bin/pytest -m live -q → 24 skipped, 408 deselected   EXIT=0
```
This requires someone to deliberately add a `skipif`, so it is a hardening note, not a defect in this PR. `pyproject.toml` also does not set `--strict-markers`; belt-and-braces given exit 5 already covers the typo case, but cheap to add.

---

## Claim 2 — NO ORPHANED TESTS: CONFIRMED

Exact three-way partition, verified by set arithmetic on collected node IDs (not by reading config). With the full CI extras plus `pyyaml`:

```
$ pytest -p no:cacheprovider --collect-only -q -m ""            → 432
$ pytest -p no:cacheprovider --collect-only -q                  → 399/432 (33 deselected)
$ pytest -p no:cacheprovider --collect-only -q -m live          →  24/432 (404 deselected)
$ pytest -p no:cacheprovider --collect-only -q -m integration   →   9/432 (419 deselected)

total=432 default=399 live=24 integration=9
union=432  sum=432
orphans (run nowhere): NONE
double-counted: NONE
```
399 + 24 + 9 = 432 = total, with union == total and pairwise intersections empty. No test file exists outside `tests/` (`testpaths = ["tests"]`).

**One real discrepancy in the author's numbers, pre-existing and not caused by this PR.** With only the extras CI installs (`.[web,dev,pdf,docx]`) the total is **428, not 432** — `tests/test_harness.py` module-skips on `pytest.importorskip("yaml")` and `pyyaml` only ships in the `harness` extra, which no CI job installs:
```
SKIPPED [1] tests/test_harness.py:22: could not import 'yaml': No module named 'yaml'
```
So the commit message / STATUS.md line "all 432 tests still run in CI" is off by 4; 428 do. The author evidently had `harness` installed locally, which is also why their counts (432 total, 391 default) don't reconcile against each other. Worth correcting in the log, but it is a pre-existing CI gap, not a regression from this change.

---

## Claim 3 — DEFAULT RUN MAKES NO NETWORK CALLS: CONFIRMED

`--allow-hosts=127.0.0.1` is a *weak* instrument in this sandbox because `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:42595` — proxied traffic looks like loopback. (Proof it's weak: `pytest -m live --allow-hosts=127.0.0.1` still passed 23/24, only arXiv failed on a direct connect to `151.101.131.42`.) So I used `--disable-socket --allow-unix-socket`, which blocks **all AF_INET socket creation** including loopback to the proxy, while permitting asyncio's internal AF_UNIX `socketpair` self-pipe that Starlette's in-process `TestClient` needs.

```
$ .venv/bin/pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket
393 passed, 3 skipped, 33 deselected, 1 warning in 2.69s     EXIT=0
```

**Negative control on the identical flags**, proving the blocker actually bites:
```
$ .venv/bin/pytest -m live -q --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket
15 failed, 9 passed, 1 skipped, 404 deselected in 10.93s
```

The default suite creates zero AF_INET sockets. The 7 `test_web.py` failures under plain `--disable-socket` are false positives from asyncio's `socketpair` self-pipe, not outbound traffic — they vanish with `--allow-unix-socket`. No non-live test reaches the network.

---

## Claim 4 — TIMING: CONFIRMED

Measured with `resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN)` around each subprocess. Pre-change baseline measured against the **actual parent-commit files** (`git checkout HEAD~1 -- pyproject.toml tests/test_checks_live.py`), not just a marker expression.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-change default (`HEAD~1` files) | 19.87s, 23.22s | 3.39s, 3.31s | 14–17% | 417 passed |
| Post-change default | 3.26 / 3.06 / 3.05s | 2.80 / 2.59 / 2.60s | 85% | 393 passed |
| `pytest -m live` | 15.48 / 15.90 / 16.81s | 1.71 / 1.91 / 1.74s | 10–12% | 24 passed |
| `pytest -m integration` | 3.29 / 3.45s | 3.29 / 3.45s | 100% | 7 passed, 2 skipped |

My numbers land on the author's: default **~20.1s → ~3.1s** (they said 20.1 → 2.7; my box is slightly slower), live **~16s** (they said 17.9s). The diagnostic that motivated the whole change reproduces exactly: the pre-change suite was **~20s wall on ~3.3s CPU (15% utilization)** — it was waiting, not computing. Post-change it's 85% CPU-bound, which independently confirms the author's call that xdist was the wrong lever.

---

## Claim 5 — COVERAGE EQUIVALENCE: **REFUTED**

The `ci.yml` comment and the test-file docstring both assert the offline files "cover every decision this module makes on its own." They do not. **160 statements in `src/slopchecker/checks/` are executed only by the live tests.**

```
$ pytest -q --cov=slopchecker.checks                      (default run)
TOTAL  1053 stmts  247 miss   77%
$ pytest -q -m "not integration" --cov=slopchecker.checks (default + live)

Per module, default → with-live:

| Module | default | +live | live-only stmts |

| `metadata_match.py` | **29%** | 84% | 47 |
| `identifiers_valid.py` | **40%** | 97% | 20 |

Root cause: **`metadata_match` and `citation_identifiers_valid` are named in exactly one test file in the whole repo — `tests/test_checks_live.py`.**
```

`test_checks_identifiers.py` exercises the `valid()` *primitive*, never the registered check that consumes it.

The `ci.yml` comment and the test-file docstring both assert the offline files "cover every decision this module makes on its own." They do not. **160 statements in `src/slopchecker/checks/` are executed only by the live tests.**

```
$ pytest -q --cov=slopchecker.checks                      (default run)
TOTAL  1053 stmts  247 miss   77%
$ pytest -q -m "not integration" --cov=slopchecker.checks (default + live)
TOTAL  1053 stmts   87 miss   92%
```

Per module, default → with-live:

| Module | default | +live | live-only stmts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metadata_match.py` | **29%** | 84% | 47 |
| `identifiers_valid.py` | **40%** | 97% | 20 |
| `providers.py` | **51%** | 82% | 48 |
| `net.py` | **53%** | 87% | 40 |

Root cause: **`metadata_match` and `citation_identifiers_valid` are named in exactly one test file in the whole repo — `tests/test_checks_live.py`.**
```
$ grep -rn "citation_identifiers_valid\|metadata_match" tests/ --include=*.py
tests/test_checks_live.py:218,221,233,240,285,288
```
`test_checks_identifiers.py` exercises the `valid()` *primitive*, never the registered check that consumes it.

### Two concrete regressions that now merge with `test` green

**(a) The #9 borrowed-DOI defect — the tool's headline capability — stops working silently.** In `src/slopchecker/checks/metadata_match.py::_examine` I changed `return compare(ref, canonical), None` to `return compare(ref, None), None`, so a real DOI pointing at a different paper always grades clean:
```
$ pytest -q      → 393 passed, 3 skipped, 33 deselected in 2.47s     ← GREEN
$ pytest -m live → 3 failed, 21 passed
    FAILED test_metadata_row_catches_the_borrowed_doi
    FAILED test_findings_name_the_planted_defects
    FAILED test_the_correctly_cited_reference_produces_no_finding
```

**(b) Malformed identifiers stop being reported at all.** In `identifiers_valid.py`, `if valid(...)` → `if True or valid(...)`:
```
$ pytest -q      → 393 passed, 3 skipped, 33 deselected in 2.58s     ← GREEN
$ pytest -m live → 2 failed, 22 passed
    FAILED test_identifier_row_counts_the_planted_malformed_pair
    FAILED test_findings_name_the_planted_defects
```

Case (b) is the sharper one: `citation_identifiers_valid` is registered **without** `needs_network=True` — it's a pure pattern check. There is no network reason for it to be untested offline. It is dark in the default suite purely because the only test that drives the registered check happens to live in the live file.

### Why this matters for the stated design intent

The PR's own justification is that `live` must stay advisory (never in the `mainsaver` ruleset) *because* the offline files gate the same behavior. That premise is false. Under this change, with #43 flipped, a PR that breaks `metadata_match` or `citation_identifiers_valid` passes the required check and merges; the only signal is an advisory job the ci.yml comment tells reviewers to treat as non-blocking and to expect red from third-party flakiness. That is precisely the shape where a real regression hides behind normalized redness.

**This does not invalidate the speedup — the mechanism is sound and claims 1–4 hold.** The fix is small and doesn't touch the marker design: move the offline half of the live file's registry-level assertions into an offline test that runs the check registry against `fixtures/checks/citations-proposal.md` with a stubbed `ProviderChain`/transport. That restores the gate for `metadata_match`, `identifiers_valid`, `_build_output`, `_finding`, `_detail` and the provider record-parsing paths without a single network call, and leaves the live file doing what it is actually for — checking that our idea of Crossref still matches Crossref. Until that lands, the `ci.yml` and docstring sentence "they cover every decision this module makes on its own" should be corrected, because someone will rely on it.

### Secondary notes (both pre-existing, neither caused by this PR)

- The author's own "side finding" that `mypy` in CI is a silent no-op is correct and independently visible (`src/slopchecker/` has no `py.typed`, step takes 0s, masked by `continue-on-error: true`).
- `tests/test_harness.py` (4 tests) never runs in any CI job — see Claim 2. Adding `harness` to the CI extras is a one-word fix.
- `ruff check src tests scripts harness` and `ruff format --check src tests` both pass on the branch.</result>

# older commit's run costs nothing. Keyed on ref, and never on main — a push
# to main should always finish and report.

  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      # uv over pip: same extras, measured 11s -> 2s on the runner (#114).
      # Astral tooling is already in the stack via ruff. --system installs into
      # the setup-python interpreter, so nothing downstream needs a venv prefix.
      #
      # `harness` is in the list because without pyyaml, tests/test_harness.py
      # module-skips on importorskip and its 4 tests run in no CI job at all
      # (#114 review).
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: pyproject.toml
      - run: uv pip install --system -e ".[web,dev,pdf,docx,similarity,harness]"
      - run: ruff check .
      # Format check is scoped to the package for now. Adopting a formatter
      # across files that predate it (scripts/) shouldn't be a side effect of
      # this PR — widen once someone reformats those with their owner's nod.

      - run: pytest
      # Full CLI chain on fabricated fixtures (#81). Deselected from the
      # default run by addopts; without this step it never runs anywhere.
      # Browser leg: ubuntu runners ship google-chrome on PATH (see #49).
      - run: pytest -m integration
      # Non-blocking to start (#2).
      - run: mypy
        continue-on-error: true

  # tests/test_checks_live.py really calls doi.org, Crossref, OpenAlex and
  # arXiv. That is deliberate and stays (a mocked resolver agrees with our
  # idea of the outside world instead of the real one) — but it was 17.6s of
  # a 20.1s unit run, essentially all network wait, so it's marked `live` and
  # deselected from the default run. This job is where it actually runs (#114).
  #
  # ⚠️ Do NOT add this job to the `mainsaver` ruleset when #43 gets flipped.
  # Its redness depends on four third-party hosts; as a merge gate, one
  # Crossref rate limit blocks the whole team. Advisory on purpose — the
  # offline files (identifiers, compare, cache, net) are what `test` gates on,
  # and they cover every decision this module makes on its own.

  # cost wall clock only against the other jobs, not against the critical path.

          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: pyproject.toml

  # which would brick the repo:

  # the dashboard — same out-of-band step #43 took for `test`.

  # filesystem, applyD1Migrations runs against Miniflare's in-process SQLite,
  # and workerd is a local binary. No Cloudflare account, no API token.

    env:
      WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS: "false"

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # sync ("No schema changes, nothing to migrate"), so any new or modified
      # file under migrations/ means drift.

            echo "Run 'npm run db:generate' in worker/ and commit the result."
            git status --porcelain migrations
            exit 1
          fi

"""Offline coverage for the registered deterministic checks (#8, #9).

Why this file exists, since it overlaps `test_checks_live.py` on purpose:

When the live tests moved behind the `live` marker (#114), review found that
`metadata_match` and `citation_identifiers_valid` were named in **no test
outside the live file**. Both are registry entries that produce ledger rows
and quote-anchored findings, and both went dark in the default suite. Breaking
either — a borrowed DOI silently grading clean, malformed identifiers silently
not reported — left `pytest` green, with the only signal in an advisory job
that reviewers are told to expect red from third-party flakiness.

So: the live file keeps proving *our idea of Crossref still matches Crossref*.
This file proves *the checks do the right thing with a record in hand*, using a
stubbed provider chain and no network at all. Two different questions; only the
second one belongs in a merge gate.

The fixture is the same planted-defect document, so the assertions read against
the same references the live tests use:
  ref[1] correct citation           ref[3] real DOI, different paper (#9)
  ref[2] unregistered DOI           ref[6] malformed ISBN, ref[7] malformed DOI
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from slopchecker.checks import identifiers_valid, metadata_match
from slopchecker.checks.providers import SourceRecord
from slopchecker.models import FlattenedDoc
from slopchecker.pipeline.registry import CheckContext

FIXTURE = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "checks" / "citations-proposal.md"

REAL_DOI = "10.1038/nature12373"

# The canonical record for REAL_DOI, as the providers really return it. Copied
# from the live tests' assertions so the two stay in agreement; if Crossref
# ever changes its answer, `pytest -m live` is what notices.
NATURE_RECORD = SourceRecord(
    provider="crossref",
    doi=REAL_DOI,
    title="Nanometre-scale thermometry in a living cell",
    surnames=("Kucsko", "Maurer", "Yao"),
    year=2013,
    venue="Nature",
)


@pytest.fixture
def doc() -> FlattenedDoc:
    raw = FIXTURE.read_bytes()
    return FlattenedDoc(
        file=FIXTURE.name,
        text=raw.decode(),
        sha256=hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
        media_type="text/markdown",
    )


class StubChain:
    """A ProviderChain that answers from a dict instead of the network.

    Only REAL_DOI has a record, mirroring reality: the fabricated DOI in the
    fixture is registered nowhere, and the reverse title search finds nothing
    for an invented paper.
    """

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.lookups: list[str] = []

    def lookup(self, client, ident):
        self.lookups.append(ident.value)
        return NATURE_RECORD if ident.value == REAL_DOI else None

    def search(self, client, *, title, surname=None, year=None):
        return None


@pytest.fixture
def offline_chain(monkeypatch) -> None:
    """Swap the provider chain and HTTP client out of `metadata_match`."""

    @contextmanager
    def no_client():
        yield None

    monkeypatch.setattr(metadata_match, "ProviderChain", StubChain)
    monkeypatch.setattr(metadata_match, "http_client", no_client)


def _row(output, check_id):
    return next(row for row in output.ledger if row.check == check_id)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# metadata_match (#9) — the borrowed-DOI defect
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_borrowed_doi_grades_as_a_different_work(doc, offline_chain) -> None:
    """#9's whole reason to exist, gated offline.

    ref[3] wears a real DOI belonging to another paper. If this check stops
    comparing the canonical record against the reference, this is the test
    that goes red — previously nothing in the default suite did.
    """
    output = metadata_match.metadata_match(doc, CheckContext(no_cache=True))
    row = _row(output, "metadata_match")

    assert row.result is False
    assert "different work" in row.detail


def test_borrowed_doi_raises_a_quote_anchored_finding(doc, offline_chain) -> None:
    finding = next(f for f in output_findings(doc) if (f.target or "").startswith("ref[3]"))
    assert finding.label == "Cited metadata describes a different work"
    assert finding.anchor is not None
    assert finding.anchor.quote in doc.text
    span = finding.anchor.span
    assert span is not None and doc.text[span.start : span.end] == finding.anchor.quote


def test_the_correctly_cited_reference_produces_no_finding(doc, offline_chain) -> None:

# 2026-07-31 — nawagner (claude-code) — CI/test speed

Issue: #114 (filed this session)

## The question

"Is there any way to make the CI tests go faster so we can increase dev
velocity?"

## What I measured before changing anything

CI wall clock across the last 25 runs was 30–90s, so CI was not slow in
absolute terms. Worth saying plainly, because the instinct at that number is
to reach for parallelism, and parallelism was the wrong lever.

Per-step timing, run 30654679072, `test` job (42s):

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| `pip install -e ".[web,dev,pdf,docx]"` | 11s |
| `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` | 1s |
| `pytest` | 20s |
| `pytest -m integration` | 4s |
| `mypy` | 0s |

`worker` (20s) runs in parallel — not the critical path, left alone.

## The finding that mattered

Locally the default suite was **20.09s wall clock but 3.9s of CPU**. That gap
is the whole story: the suite was not computing, it was waiting. `--durations`
put ~17s of it in one file, `tests/test_checks_live.py`, which really calls
doi.org, Crossref, OpenAlex and arXiv.

Deleting that file from the run: **20.09s → 2.48s**, 391 tests still passing.

The live tests are deliberate and good — a mocked resolver agrees with our
idea of the outside world instead of the real one, which is the entire point
of the deterministic tier. They should keep running. They just should not sit
in the loop a developer hits dozens of times an hour.

The file's own docstring had already specced the fix and I took it nearly
verbatim, only preferring a marker over the `SLOPCHECK_LIVE=1` env var it
suggested, so it matches how `test_integration_e2e.py` already handles
`integration` (one mechanism, not two).

## What landed

1. **`pytestmark = pytest.mark.live`** on `tests/test_checks_live.py`;
   `addopts = "-m 'not integration and not live'"`; marker registered.
2. **Own CI job** (`live`), parallel with `test`, running `pytest -m live`.
3. **pip → uv** — measured 2.0s vs 18.0s cold on the same extras.
4. **`concurrency:` group** with cancel-in-progress everywhere except main.

## Why a separate job, not just a separate step

A separate *step* in `test` would have fixed the local loop but saved no CI
wall clock, and would have left the important problem in place. #43 is about
to make `test` a required check. Live tests inside a required check means a
Crossref rate limit or a doi.org blip blocks every merge on the repo. As its
own advisory job, an outage reds `live` and nothing else.

There is a comment in `ci.yml` saying so, because the failure mode here is
someone helpfully adding `live` to the `mainsaver` ruleset later and
reintroducing exactly the problem this removed.

## Results

- Local default `pytest`: **20.1s → 2.7s**
- Expect `test` job ~42s → ~10s; CI wall clock bounded by `live` (~25s)
- Coverage unchanged — all 432 tests still run in CI

## Dead ends / deliberate non-goals

- **pytest-xdist.** The reflexive fix, and wrong here. Post-gating the suite
  is 2.5s wall / 2.3s CPU; xdist worker startup would eat most of a 4-core
  runner's gain. Recorded in the issue so nobody re-derives it.
- **`paths:` filters** to skip jobs — `ci.yml` already warns why (a required
  check that never runs leaves a PR permanently pending). Didn't touch it.
- **Matrix on `test`** — same warning, renames the check. Adding a sibling
  job is safe; `test` keeps its name.
- **Caching the live responses** (VCR/cassettes) — considered and rejected.
  It would make them fast but would convert them into exactly the mocked
  tests the file exists to avoid. The value is that they can fail when the
  outside world changes.

## Side finding, not fixed

`mypy` in CI does nothing. `src/slopchecker/` has no `py.typed`, so mypy exits

```
$ grep -rn "citation_identifiers_valid\|metadata_match" tests/ --include=*.py
tests/test_checks_live.py:218,221,233,240,285,288
```

`test_checks_identifiers.py` exercises the `valid()` *primitive*, never the registered check consuming it. So gating the live file out of `test` meant two real regressions merged green:

| Sabotage | `pytest` | `pytest -m live` |
|---|---|---|
| Neuter the borrowed-DOI comparison (#9's headline capability) | **green** ✅ | 3 failed |
| Stop reporting malformed identifiers | **green** ✅ | 2 failed |

That is precisely the shape a regression hides in — the only signal is an advisory job that the `ci.yml` comment tells reviewers to expect red from third-party flakiness. Worse, **this PR's argument for keeping `live` advisory depended on the premise being true.** It wasn't. I asserted it from the file's docstring instead of checking it.

`tests/test_checks_registered.py` — both registered checks driven against a stubbed `ProviderChain`, no network, 8 tests in 0.2s. Verified by replaying both sabotages; each now reds the default suite:

FAILED tests/test_checks_registered.py::test_borrowed_doi_raises_a_quote_anchored_finding

FAILED tests/test_checks_registered.py::test_malformed_findings_name_their_targets

|---|---|---|

The residual (`providers.py`, `net.py`) stays live-only, which is correct — that code is about whether our idea of Crossref still matches Crossref, and no merge gate should depend on Crossref being up.

Both the `ci.yml` comment and the live-file docstring asserted the false claim; both now state what's true and why it must stay true ("a registered check whose only coverage lives here is a check that is not actually gated").

Found while rebasing #117 onto main. Filing rather than fixing — this crosses `pipeline/` (Dan) and the CLI/web layer, and #117 is already scoped to CI speed.

## What

#114 took ~17.6s of network wait out of the default suite by gating the live tests. Rebasing onto current main, the default suite is slow again — for a different reason, through a different door.

`--durations` on current main:

```
2.35s call tests/test_web.py::test_check_json_format_returns_report_dict
2.19s call tests/test_web.py::test_check_renders_html_report
1.90s call tests/test_cli_run.py::test_report_json_feeds_render_command
1.86s call tests/test_cli_run.py::test_run_html_format
1.83s call tests/test_cli_run.py::test_run_writes_json_report_and_summary
1.83s call tests/test_cli_run.py::test_solicitation_recorded
1.81s call tests/test_cli_run.py::test_findings_never_fail_the_exit_code
1.81s call tests/test_cli_run.py::test_batch_records_ingest_gaps_alongside_reports
1.78s call tests/test_cli_run.py::test_run_reads_pdf_end_to_end
1.77s call tests/test_web.py::test_check_hostile_filename_is_flattened
```

Roughly **19s across ~10 tests**. Before #96 these same tests were ~0.06s.

## It's network, and it buys nothing

Blocking DNS and re-running two of them — they get ~20x faster **and still pass**:

```
$ python3 -c "import socket; socket.getaddrinfo = socket.create_connection = <raise>; pytest ..."
0.11s call tests/test_cli_run.py::test_run_writes_json_report_and_summary   (was 2.35s)
0.06s call tests/test_web.py::test_check_renders_html_report                (was 2.19s)
2 passed in 0.58s
```

Identical assertions, identical outcome. The network calls contribute nothing — the tests are just waiting on doi.org/Crossref for results they never assert on.

## Cause

#96 registered citations + Pangram as pipeline checks. Every CLI/web test that runs the pipeline end-to-end now executes the deterministic tier, which does real DOI/URL resolution. The tests aren't asking for that; they're checking CLI exit codes, JSON shape, and HTML rendering.

This isn't a criticism of #96 — registering the checks is right. The gap is that the CLI/web tests exercise a pipeline that now reaches the network by default, and nobody asked them to.

## Options

1. **Give the CLI/web tests a context that skips network-tier checks** — a `CheckContext` flag or `--tier` selection so they run the offline tier only. Most surgical; keeps them testing what they're actually about.
2. **Stub the resolver at the seam** for these tests, the way `test_checks_registered.py` (from #117) stubs `ProviderChain`.
3. **Mark them `live`.** Cheapest, but wrong — they'd stop gating CLI/web behavior in the required check, which is the mistake #117's review just caught me making elsewhere.

I'd take (1), with (2) as fallback.

## Suggested guard

Worth considering a blanket `--disable-socket --allow-unix-socket` (pytest-socket) on the default run, so "a unit test reached the network" fails loudly instead of just costing 2s. Verified during #117's review that the default suite passes clean under exactly those flags — the `--allow-unix-socket` part is needed for asyncio's internal `socketpair` self-pipe that Starlette's `TestClient` uses. That would make this class of regression impossible to reintroduce silently, which matters because it has now happened twice.
